prompt:
Research what the SQLite project officially documents about the maximum database size and maximum row size. Cite the official SQLite limits page and quote the figures.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "The theoretical maximum number of rows in a table is 264 (18446744073709551616 or about 1.8e+19)." | CLAIM: The maximum number of rows in a SQLite table is 2^64.
SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "This limit is unreachable since the maximum database size of 281 terabytes will be reached first." | CLAIM: The maximum database size is 281 terabytes (which is reached before the theoretical row limit).
SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "The default setting for SQLITE_MAX_COLUMN is 2000." | CLAIM: The default maximum number of columns in a table is 2000.
SOURCE: https://www.sqlite.org/limits.html | QUOTE: "You can raise it at compile time to as large as 32767." | CLAIM: The maximum number of columns can be increased to 32767 at compile time.
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: The maximum size of a single row (in bytes) on the SQLite limits page.
